ཏེ་བསྟན་པའོ། །དེ་ཡན་ཆད་ཀྱིས་#སྡུད་པ་པོས་བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཆེ་བ་དང་ལེའུའི་བརྗོད་པར་བྱ་བའི་དོན་མན་ངག་དང་བཅས་པར་བསྟན་ཏོ། །སྐུ་གསུང་ཐུགས་གཅིག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པས་ཀྱང་ཞེས་པ་ནི་དོན་དམ་པར་དངོས་པོ་ཐམས་ཅད་རྣམ་པར་དཔྱད་ན་ཐ་དད་པར་མི་དམིགས་
ཏེ། གང་ཞིག་རང་གི་རྒྱུད་ལ་གནས་པ་དེ་ཉིད་གཞན་གྱི་རྒྱུད་ལ་གནས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །འོན་ཀྱང་བསྒྲུབ་པར་བྱ་བ་དང་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད་པའི་བྱེ་བྲག་ལ་དམིགས་ཏེ་གློ་བུར་གྱི་དྲི་མ་ལྡོག་པའི་དོན་དུ་ཚར་གཅོད་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་སྒྲུབ་པ་པོས་བསྒྲུབ་བྱ་ལ་ཚར་གཅོད་པར་བྱེད་པའོ། །དེ་ཡང་ཉེ་བར་
མཚོན་པའི་ཚིག་ཡིན་ཏེ་ཞི་བ་ལ་སོགས་པས་ཀྱང་རྗེས་སུ་གཟུང་བར་མཛད་པའོ། །ཨཱ་ལི་ཀཱ་ལི་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པས་དེ་ལྟར་གྱུར་པ་སྐུ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རང་བཞིན་སྔགས་ཐམས་ཅད་བསྡུ་བར་བྱེད་པའི་ཡི་གེ་གསུམ་གྱིས་#སྤེལ་བའི་སྔགས་ཀྱིས་#ཞི་བ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ལས་ཀྱི་

...is taught. Up to this point, the **Compiler** has shown the greatness of the self and the subject matter of the chapter along with the oral instructions. Regarding the phrase "because the body, speech, and mind have become one," it means that if all things are analyzed from the perspective of ultimate reality, they are not perceived as separate. That which dwells in one’s own continuum is precisely what dwells in the continuum of another. However, based on the distinction between the object to be accomplished and the accomplisher, "subjugation" for the sake of reversing adventitious stains means the practitioner subjugates the object to be accomplished. This is also a symbolic term; through peaceful activities and so forth, they are also cared for. Regarding the phrase "A-li Ka-li" <note>vowels and consonants</note> and so forth, it shows the meditative concentration that is beautiful because it completes the collection of activities such as peaceful ones through mantras interspersed with the three syllables <note>Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ</note> which condense all mantras of the nature of the body and so forth. "That which shows it" refers to whatever collection of sounds clarifies it in that way. Regarding "explained with intention," this is because reality is shown through the gateway of contradictory language. From the *Tikā Commentary Clarifying the Lamp* <note>original: "sgron ma gsal bar byེད་ pa'i 'grel pa'i ṭī kā"</note>, this concludes the extensive explanation of the fourteenth chapter.

The explanation of the fifteenth chapter begins with the phrase "The explained and the unexplained" and so forth. The intention is this: what was "explained" was taught in the thirteenth and fourteenth chapters. What was "unexplained" are the collections of activities to be explained in the fifteenth, sixteenth, and seventeenth chapters; because these will not be accomplished without the illusion-like meditative concentration, the fifteenth chapter is taught. Regarding the phrase "possessing the nature of the four emptinesses," these are: emptiness, extreme emptiness, great emptiness, and all-emptiness. Alternatively: appearance, increase of appearance, near-attainment of appearance, and clear light. Alternatively: the four channels within the lotus. The "self" <note>essence</note> is the central channel, the "parasol of desire." As it is said:

Thus far, the compiler has shown the greatness of himself and the subject matter of the chapter along with the oral instructions. Regarding "because body, speech, and mind have become one," this means that from the perspective of ultimate reality, if all phenomena are analyzed, no difference is perceived. That which resides in one's own continuum is the very thing that resides in the continuum of others. However, with regard to the distinction between the object to be accomplished and the accomplisher, "subduing" for the sake of reversing adventitious stains means the practitioner subdues the object of accomplishment. Furthermore, this is a figurative expression; they are also cared for through pacifying activities and so forth. 

By the phrase "vowels and consonants" <term>āli-kāli</term> and so forth, it is shown that the state of meditative concentration, which is beautiful because of the perfection of the collection of activities such as pacifying, is achieved through mantras interlaced with the three syllables <note>OM AH HUM</note> that condense all mantras which are the nature of the body and so forth. Regarding "that which illustrates it," this refers to the collection of sounds which clearly manifest that state. Regarding "explained with intentional meaning," this is because reality is shown through the gateway of "twilight language" <note>intentional or paradoxical language</note>. 

From the *Tīkā* commentary on the *Clear Lamp* <term>Pradīpodyotana</term>, this is the extensive explanation of the fourteenth chapter. 

Regarding "the explained and the unexplained" and so forth, the explanation of the fifteenth chapter begins. The intent is as follows: "the explained" refers to what was taught in the thirteenth and fourteenth chapters. "The unexplained" refers to those collections of activities that will be explained in the fifteenth, sixteenth, and seventeenth chapters. Because these will not be accomplished without the "illusion-like meditative concentration," the fifteenth chapter is taught. Regarding "possessing the nature of the four empties," these are: empty, very empty, great empty, and all-empty. Alternatively: appearance, increase of appearance, near-attainment of appearance, and clear light. Alternatively, these are the four channels within the lotus.
